text:
Why Apple Could Have Another Massive Run Soon
Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) is looking to create the next explosive technology boom.
By all indications, the field it’s betting big on is augmented reality (AR).
Apple’s next move is to use the lessons from the AR-enabled iPhone 8 to create a new device — one specifically designed to take FULL advantage of everything AR has to offer.
I’m talking about AR headsets and glasses like Microsoft’s HoloLens.
Here’s a pic of my colleague taking in AR tech first hand:
If I’m right and Apple does announce a plan to create an AR headset, expect a buying frenzy for the stock.
The AR market is currently worth about $2.6 billion. But some experts believe it could be worth as much as $7 trillion by 2027.
That’s a potential jump of 269,130% in a decade. And a chance for you to see an oversized payday before the uptrend goes vertical.
When Apple announced its latest iteration of the iPhone 8, it was made with the intent to bring AR technology to the masses.
But there was still a major limitation — you still have to hold your phone in front of your face to benefit from AR. You need your camera to look around, and you’ll have to stare at your phone’s screen to see the information.
A wearable headset will alleviate those problems. AR headsets and smart glasses essentially function as a smartphone, but rather than fiddling with a phone and taking up the use of your hands, the glasses project their software applications right on the lenses. Information is superimposed over what you are actually seeing.
But this means displays have to have high resolution. Batteries have to be light and powerful. And there has to be a way for users to interact with a wearable AR device.
Another important advance includes new voice recognition chip hardware. This is needed for users to be able to send commands to AR smart glasses under real-world conditions, and not rely on a clunky keyboard to interact with AR software.
And these advances in AR tech are exactly what Apple engineers are working on.
With Apple’s interest in dominating this sector of the market, AR is reaching an inflection point for investors.
An Apple AR headset is inevitable… And if it hits with consumers, watch Apple’s share value soar! AAPL , Apple , augmented reality , HoloLens , iPhone 8 , Microsoft , Nasdaq About Ray Blanco:
